_comment: Thumbnail options from a film's own stills (scripts/_thumb.py, scripts/thumb-options.py, studio/thumbs.py). Geometry is in the 1920x1080 design space the options are written at. Every threshold names where it came from; the ones marked _measured were set by the bake-off in docs/reference.md 'Thumbnail options'.
_max_bytes: YouTube takes 50 MB from a desktop or the API but still 2 MB from a phone (support.google.com/youtube/answer/72431); a 1080p JPEG at q90 is ~0.3-0.8 MB, so the phone limit is the one kept.

safe._source: No official spec. Practitioner rules (thumix.com/blog/youtube-thumbnail-safe-zone, ytdetective.com): ~5% margins, keep text out of the bottom-right ~15% where the duration stamp sits, and the bottom ~3% where the watched-progress bar sits.

feed._source: 168x94 is the desktop up-next sidebar, the smallest place a video's thumbnail is shown with its title (thumbnailcreator.com, collabpals.com). A cap height of ~8 px there is the floor for reading a word at a glance: 1920 -> 168 is an 11.4x reduction, so the words need a cap height of >= 92 px at 1080p.
feed._measured: Bake-off 2026-09-29, 8 studio films (crayon, clean, blueprint, painted, Ukrainian), 32 options from Claude's own concepts: every worded option set at a cap height of 8.4-17.5 px at 168 px wide; RapidOCR read every word back on all 21 Latin-script ones at 168, 246 and 360 px, the smallest included -- the gate is not too lax. Cyrillic is out of that OCR's reach (it reads the shapes as Latin lookalikes), so only the cap height vouches for it.

_contrast_min: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 (w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html): 4.5:1 for text, measured between the letters and the ring of pixels immediately around them on the finished picture -- which is the outline where there is one.

words._source: Paddy Galloway's glance test: title and thumbnail are one unit and should complement, not repeat. 'Under 4 words' is a practitioner default, not a measured fact.

fonts._comment: Tried in order; the first whose glyphs cover every character of the words is used. Anton has no Cyrillic, so a Ukrainian line falls through to Montserrat.

headline._measured: quiet_max is the mean detail (|dx|+|dy| of the grey frame at 1/8 scale) under a text-sized block above which the words get a scrim. Measured over the moment stills of 8 studio films (2026-09-29): a 320x160 block on an empty ground scores 0.001-0.02, a busy one 0.04-0.13; painted films sit at 0.05-0.09 through most of the frame. cover_max is the share of the frame's subject saliency the words may hide.

still._why: A still is pushed in (subject as large as possible, YouTube Help 12340300) only when the crop keeps 97% of the frame's subject saliency; otherwise it is shown whole.

grade._why: Colourfulness and brightness predict how much of a branded video people watch (Koh & Cui 2022, Decision Support Systems 157). A light lift only: the films' flat fills clip if it is pushed.

settle._why: A frame is settled when the film looks the same 0.2 s either side of it: a crossfade, a line still drawing itself or a camera move all differ there. Among the settled ones, a thin frame (a scene not drawn in yet, a fade) loses to a fuller one.
settle._measured: Same bake-off: YouTube-like frames at 25/50/75% of the film caught it moving (mean difference over +-0.2 s above 0.03) 10 times in 24; the settled frames 6 in 32, median movement 0.0149 -> 0.0054.

concepts._min_gap: The same as the moments sheet's own spacing: four picks from the sheet are four different frames. It was 2 s, which the sheet itself breaks (moments 1 s apart), and the first real draft spent a second call on it (2026-09-29).

_places: Where a writer may ask the words to go, as fractions of the frame [x0, y0, x1, y1]; the margins and the duration badge are cut out of each. There is no bottom-right: that is where YouTube stamps the duration.

text._measured: OCR (RapidOCR, local) finds the words a film draws -- headings, thin labels, handwriting, Cyrillic, a rotated bottle label -- in 0.2-0.7 s a frame at half size (6 frames of 6 films, 2026-09-29). Boxes are grown by grow_px; a box read with less than min_score confidence is texture, not words. hide_max_px allows a drop shadow's fringe.
text._min_h_px: Measured on 7 frames of 6 films (2026-09-29): an app screen's own print is 22-30 px tall at 1080p, the labels and captions people read 34-70 px (a wine's tasting notes 34-42, a diagram's labels 52-66), headings 70-116.

_contrast_measured: Same bake-off: contrast of the 24 worded options 4.81-12.4:1, median 9.07.
